reconstructed_article: The Victorian Government has approved a $380 million wind farm at Mount Gellibrand in the state's south-west. Planning Minister Rob Hulls announced the decision. The project is described as Australia's most powerful and Victoria's largest wind farm to date. It is expected to create between 110 and 120 jobs during construction and up to 25 full-time positions during operation. The wind farm will be located 120 km west of Melbourne, close to Colac. It will comprise 116 turbines of the 2 MW class, with an overall capacity of 232 MW. The facility is expected to produce over 700,000 MWh annually, enough to supply approximately 132,000 Victorian households. German company Pro Ventum International is undertaking the project. Minister Hulls said nine objections had been lodged against the project. Local landowner Tim Gore, who plans to have 32 turbines on his property, said he was not concerned about potential noise. Pro Ventum International said it would commence work on an Environmental Management report in the coming weeks. Wind farm critic Tim Le Roy said there was no environmental benefit from the project and the Victorian Government would better spend its money elsewhere. In October of the previous year, Colac Otway council chief executive officer Tracey Slatter said the proposal would benefit the shire by reducing greenhouse gas emissions and addressing increasing energy demand.

reconstructed_article: The Freewinds, a ship owned by the Church of Scientology, was sealed in April 2008 at Curaçao, where public health officials began an investigation into the presence of blue asbestos. According to The Daily Herald and Lloyd's List, work on the ship's interior was suspended on April 27 after health inspectors found traces of blue asbestos. Samples taken from paneling were sent to the Netherlands, where analysis revealed significant levels of blue asbestos. An April 25 inspection involved Frank Esser, interim director of the Curaçao Drydock Company; Christiene van der Biezen, Curaçao's head of labor affairs; Tico Ras, head of the local health department; and two inspectors. Panama Maritime Authority director Alfonso Castillero stated an investigation was underway. Lawrence Woodcraft, a former Scientologist and licensed architect, supervised work on the ship in 1987 and attested to the presence of blue asbestos in a 2001 online statement. He reported his findings to Church of Scientology executives at the time. The Church of Scientology purchased the ship, then known as the Bohème, in 1987 through Flag Ship Trust, and put it into service in June 1988 for advanced Scientology training and spiritual retreats. Church spokeswoman Karin Pouw stated that air quality inspections in April confirmed the Freewinds meets U.S. standards. The Church of Scientology dispatched a team from the United States to Curaçao to remove asbestos. A May 15 statement to a UK newspaper said there has never been asbestos exposure on the Freewinds.

reconstructed_article: On Friday, 178 plaintiffs, including construction workers and family members of deceased workers, filed a lawsuit in Tokyo, Japan, seeking approximately 6.6 billion yen (about 64 million USD) in damages from the Japanese government and 46 building manufacturers. According to reports, the class action is the first in Japan related to health damages caused by asbestos exposure at construction sites. The plaintiffs are from Tokyo and surrounding areas. They claim that the government and manufacturers knew of the dangers of asbestos inhalation but failed to take proper precautions, including ceasing to promote asbestos as a cheap construction material and banning its production. After inhaling asbestos in the workplace, 172 people developed lung cancer or mesothelioma, and nearly half of those afflicted have died. Plaintiffs argue that the government and health ministry did not act quickly enough after international organizations issued warnings in 1972 that asbestos could be a carcinogen. They also blame the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry for sanctioning asbestos use under the Factory Act, and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism for approving asbestos-containing materials under Japan's Building Standards Law. Approximately 40 construction workers plan to file a similar lawsuit in June. Following a 2005 revelation that residents near a factory developed asbestos-related diseases, the government implemented a 2006 law providing monetary assistance to victims and relatives. Plaintiffs argue the assistance is insufficient. Japan had already banned the spraying of asbestos in 1975.

reconstructed_article: On Friday, 178 plaintiffs, including construction workers and family members of deceased workers, filed a lawsuit in Tokyo, Japan, seeking approximately 6.6 billion yen (about 64 million USD) in damages from the Japanese government and 46 building manufacturers. They claim that the government and manufacturers were aware of the dangers of asbestos inhalation but did not take adequate precautions, including ceasing to promote asbestos as a cheap construction material and banning its production. After inhaling asbestos in the workplace, 172 people developed lung cancer or mesothelioma, and nearly half of those afflicted have died. Plaintiffs argue that the government and health ministry did not act swiftly enough after international organizations issued warnings in 1972 that asbestos could be a carcinogen. Approximately 40 construction workers plan to file a similar lawsuit in June. Following a 2005 revelation that residents near a factory developed asbestos-related diseases, the government implemented a 2006 law providing monetary assistance to victims and relatives. Plaintiffs argue the assistance is insufficient. Japan had already taken the step of banning the spraying of asbestos in 1975.

reconstructed_article: On Tuesday at approximately 4:00 a.m., around 500 melon-headed whales were spotted swimming near the shores of Pilar, Bataan, approximately 135 kilometers northwest of Manila. Philippine Coast Guard commander Luis Tuazon and Bataan Governor Enrique Garcia Jr. reported the sighting. More than 100 fishermen and volunteers, along with personnel from the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), local police, and the Coast Guard, used dozens of fishing boats with engines shut off to guide the whales toward deeper waters by clapping and hitting the water surface. The mammals were initially identified as dolphins but were later identified as melon-headed whales by local veterinarian Mariel Flores. Four dead whales were found in Abucay and Tortugas, including two adult females, one pregnant and one that had given birth to a calf that also died. A necropsy by Dr. Lemnuel Aragones of the University of the Philippines found the two adults had damaged eardrums. Provincial veterinarian Alberto Venturina said the adults weighed 250 to 300 kilograms, and the calf was approximately one month old. BFAR director Malcolm Sarmiento Jr. noted this was the largest stranding recorded, with previous events involving only 20 to 30 animals. By 4:30 p.m., the whales were guided back to deeper waters. Possible causes discussed included underwater earthquakes, chemical pollution, dynamite fishing, and a sea floor earthquake study conducted by the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. PHIVOLCS reported no significant seismic events at the time.

More than 100 fishermen and volunteers, along with personnel from the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), local police, and the Coast Guard, deployed dozens of fishing boats with engines shut off in an effort to guide the whales toward deeper waters by clapping and hitting the water surface. Provincial veterinarian Alberto Venturina said the adults weighed 250 to 300 kilograms, and the calf was approximately one month old. BFAR director Malcolm Sarmiento Jr. noted this was the worst stranding recorded, with previous events involving only 20 to 30 animals. By 4:30 p.m., the whales were guided back to deeper waters. Possible causes discussed included underwater earthquakes, chemical pollution, dynamite fishing, and a sea floor earthquake study conducted by the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. PHIVOLCS reported no significant seismic events at the time.

reconstructed_article: On Friday, the discovery of airborne asbestos in Renaissance Middle School in Montclair, New Jersey, prompted the evacuation of over 200 students and the school's closure. The school, part of Montclair Public Schools, was closed Monday and remained closed Tuesday while undergoing asbestos testing and cleaning. According to a letter sent to parents by the Superintendent's Office of Montclair Public Schools, plaster may have been disturbed during construction on new fire doors on Thursday. An inspection arranged by the school district indicated asbestos was present in the plaster, and a subsequent inspection by asbestos consultant Detail Associates revealed airborne asbestos fiber levels exceeding the acceptable range in the third floor hallway. Business administrator Dana Sullivan stated that testing on March 31 confirmed asbestos in a brown undercoating of plaster. The affected area was sealed off. Public Information Officer Laura Federico said sixth and seventh graders were transported to Hillside Elementary School and eighth graders to another location. Detail Associates conducted cleaning on Saturday. At a Monday meeting between parents and district officials, parents demanded lockers be included in cleanup, prompting Tuesday's closure. Steve Jaraczewski of Detail Associates said one of four test samples was positive for airborne asbestos at over six times acceptable levels. He criticized the inadequate asbestos management plan provided by the Archdiocese of Newark, which owns the building. Archdiocese representative Jim Goodness stated the building would reopen soon. The state Department of Environmental Protection is supervising the cleanup.

reconstructed_article: Thirteen Asian countries saw ministers pledge on Friday to double the wild tiger population on the continent to seven thousand by 2022. The commitment was made in Thailand at Asia's first ministerial conference on tiger conservation. The thirteen countries that endorsed the pledge were Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Russia, Thailand, and Vietnam, all countries where the wild Asian tiger is still found. Thai Prime Minister Abhisit Vejjajiva stated in a video address that the wild tiger is in crisis and that this may be the last chance to save it. The meeting was partially organized by the Global Tiger Initiative, a coalition within the World Bank, as well as the Smithsonian Institution and various conservation groups. Meeting host Suwit Khunkitti, Thailand's minister of natural resources and environment, noted that there were 100,000 tigers across range countries 100 years ago, compared to about 3,500 today. According to the World Wildlife Fund (WWF), tiger numbers have declined due to poaching. The animals live in only seven percent of the territory they occupied a hundred years ago, according to Voice of America. WWF representative Michael Baltzer said it was important to act during the Year of the Tiger. Global Tiger Initiative program director Keshav Varma said saving the tiger also preserves habitat for other species and draws attention to issues including encroachment and corruption.

reconstructed_article: Ministers from thirteen Asian countries pledged on Friday to double the wild tiger population on the continent to seven thousand by 2022. The commitment was made in Thailand at Asia's first ministerial conference on tiger conservation. Thai Prime Minister Abhisit Vejjajiva stated in a video address that the wild tiger is in crisis and that this may be the last chance to save it. The meeting was partially organized by the Global Tiger Initiative, a coalition within the World Bank, as well as the Smithsonian Institution and various conservation groups. Meeting host Suwit Khunkitti, Thailand's minister of natural resources and environment, noted that there were 100,000 tigers across range countries 100 years ago, compared to about 3,500 today. According to the World Wildlife Fund (WWF), tiger numbers have declined due to poaching. The animals live in only seven percent of the territory they occupied a hundred years ago, according to Voice of America. WWF representative Michael Baltzer said it was important to act during the Year of the Tiger. Global Tiger Initiative program director Keshav Varma said saving the tiger also preserves habitat for other species and draws attention to issues including encroachment and corruption.

reconstructed_article: Senator Campbell praised supermarket shoppers and operators for reducing plastic bag use by three billion bags over the past two years. A report compiled by a body representing major supermarkets showed that by the end of last year, supermarkets had reduced their annual use of lightweight, single-use bags by 45 per cent compared with 2002. Senator Campbell said the cutback means fewer bags in the litter stream and that the goal is to stop plastic bags entering the litter stream and spoiling Australia's environment. He said the result came from voluntary action, with no regulations, levies, or additional costs to shoppers. Major supermarkets are now committed to achieving a 50 per cent reduction goal by the end of this year. Campbell also said development of a viable degradable bag to replace existing lightweight plastic ones is key to further reductions. Environmentalists say plastic bags have had a severe impact on Australia's natural environment. Plastic bags can take between 20 and 1000 years to break down. An estimated 6.67 billion or 36,700 tonnes of plastic bags are disposed of in landfill sites throughout Australia each year. Many thousands of marine mammals and seabirds die every year worldwide as a result of plastic litter. A 2004 NSW Parliamentary paper reported that plastic bags are of significant concern in the marine and aquatic environment, as aquatic life can be threatened through entanglement, suffocation, and ingestion.

He vetoed a bill that would have allowed illegal immigrants to receive driver's licenses and signed another requiring identification to vote. During his presidential campaign, Perry opposed the proposed full-length border fence, calling it impractical. He favors targeted fencing combined with mobilization of enforcement personnel.

reconstructed_article:
The Australian Government is constructing a $210 million, 800-bed detention facility on Christmas Island, 1400km off Australia's northwest coast. Construction began in January 2005, with the facility scheduled to be operational by late 2006. A DIMIA spokesperson stated the facility would serve as an immigration reception and processing centre, and that a review of mainland detention centres would likely follow its completion.

Christmas Island Shire President Gordon Thompson said residents were concerned about impacts on tourism, restricted access to fishing and snorkelling areas, and lack of consultation. He said the Shire council was not notified when the existing Christmas Island detention centre reopened on November 17 to detain seven West Timorese asylum seekers. Azmi Yon, president of the island's Malay association, said locals sought written clarification on the facility's purpose.

Democrats senator Andrew Bartlett said transferring asylum seekers to the remote location denied them proper processing and legal access. Greens senator Kerry Nettle called for construction to be suspended, citing existing detention capacity of 3,975 people across facilities including Baxter, Villawood, Maribyrnong, Perth, Port Augusta, Port Hedland, and Woomera.

Environmental concerns were raised because the site is adjacent to Abbott's Booby habitat within Christmas Island National Park. Research indicated nesting birds within 300 metres of clearings experienced lower breeding success, with 36% of breeding sites in that zone. The Wilderness Society criticised the government's decision to exempt itself from EPBC Act environmental scrutiny.

Construction began in January 2005, with the facility scheduled to be operational by late 2006.

Christmas Island Shire President Gordon Thompson said residents were concerned about impacts on tourism, restricted access to fishing and snorkelling areas, and lack of consultation. He said the Shire council was not notified when the existing Christmas Island detention centre reopened on November 17 to detain seven West Timorese asylum seekers. Azmi Yon, president of the island's Malay association, said locals sought written clarification on the facility's purpose.

Democrats senator Andrew Bartlett said transferring asylum seekers to the remote location denied them proper processing and legal access. Greens senator Kerry Nettle called for construction to be suspended, citing existing detention capacity of 3,975 people across facilities including Baxter, Villawood, Maribyrnong, Perth, Port Augusta, Port Hedland, and Woomera.

Environmental concerns were raised because the site is adjacent to Abbott's Booby habitat within Christmas Island National Park. Research indicated nesting birds within 300 metres of clearings experienced lower breeding success, with 36% of breeding sites in that zone. The Wilderness Society criticised the government's self-exemption from EPBC Act environmental scrutiny.

reconstructed_article:
Democrats.com, a progressive organization, is offering a $1,000 reward to anyone who can get U.S. President George W. Bush to answer a question about pre-war intelligence. The offer follows Bush's month-long refusal to answer questions about a leaked secret memo stating that "the intelligence and facts were being fixed around the policy." Neither the U.S. nor UK government has disputed the document's accuracy. The question asks whether Bush and his administration "fixed" intelligence about Iraqi weapons of mass destruction and terrorism ties to justify the invasion of Iraq. An additional $100 is offered to anyone who asks Bush the question, with video evidence required. The reward money came from modest donations to the website.

The contest occurs amid renewed criticism from citizens, members of Congress, retired politicians, and constitutional lawyers following the leak of British documents. Earlier in the month, White House spokesman Scott McClellan told reporters the administration saw "no need" to respond to a congressional letter about the memo, stating that public comments before the war showed how intelligence was used. One pre-war justification was that Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction, none of which were found. The Senate Intelligence Committee is considering three possibilities: the weapons were moved, CIA intelligence was flawed, or satisfactory intelligence was mishandled by the administration. The last possibility has not been formally investigated.

reconstructed_article: The People's Alliance for Democracy (PAD), a Thai anti-government movement, conducted a campaign of disruption called the 'King Taksin operation,' named after an 18th-century Siamese monarch. PAD protesters began gathering on Sunday and blockaded the parliament building on Monday morning, leading to the cancellation of joint MP and Senate sessions. The PAD said it would continue disrupting parliamentary sessions until parliament went into recess or the government resigned. The PAD opposes proposed constitutional changes. The government said these changes were not on Monday's agenda and that ASEAN-related legislation was scheduled for discussion instead. Thailand, the current chair of ASEAN, faced concerns about its ability to ratify treaties at an upcoming meeting in northern Thailand. With parliament inactive, PAD protesters targeted additional government offices, including the temporary cabinet location at the old Bangkok international airport. The government had operated from mothballed buildings there since the PAD took over the main Government House compound in late August. A PAD call for a public sector strike drew limited response. The government of Prime Minister Somchai Wongsawat of the People Power Party (PPP) was the target. Authorities avoided confrontation following clashes the previous month in which two protesters were killed when police used tear gas. Police allowed protesters to lay siege to the empty parliament building. Deposed former Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra, in self-imposed exile and facing a two-year prison sentence in Thailand, said in an interview with Abu Dhabi's Arabian Business that he intended to return to politics. He condemned the UK government for revoking his visa. He was believed to be staying in Dubai.

reconstructed_article: Corus, the world's fifth largest steel producer, announced on Friday that it may be forced to mothball its steelworks in Teesside, England, threatening the jobs of 1,920 employees. Corus said a consortium had refused to honour a 10-year contract with Corus' Teesside Cast Products, which accounted for 78% of the plant's operations. Corus' chief executive, Kirby Adams, said he was extremely disappointed that the consortium members had taken this action. Business Secretary Peter Mandelson said it is essential that Corus does everything it can legally, and with the government's assistance, to reinstate the agreement. British Prime Minister Gordon Brown said the government was doing everything in its power to ensure that the contract is upheld. Mandelson also said the government was not prepared to reconcile itself to the inevitable closure of the plant. The leader of Redcar and Cleveland Council, Councillor George Dunning, described the announcement as being hit by a mini earthquake. Liberal Democrats including Simon Hughes, Fiona Hall, and Stephen Hughes MEP supported the idea that the government should subsidise wages at the plant on a temporary basis. Hughes and Hall suggested the government should apply to the EU's European Globalisation Fund. Adams said the move could bring to an end a proud heritage of steelmaking at Teesside. Corus said a 90-day consultation period is due to begin. Corus' owner, Tata Steel, is also facing difficulties with another UK operation, automobile company Jaguar Land Rover.

reconstructed_article: Sam Savarino, developer and CEO of Savarino Companies, confirmed that he has purchased a severely damaged stable and livery on Buffalo's West Side from owner Bob Freudenheim for $1.00 and plans to restore it. The building partially collapsed on June 11, causing 15 homes to be evacuated. Savarino stated he hopes to save the facade, at least 20 feet of the side walls, all of the back walls including the elevator tower, and if possible all three floors. He inherits a tax lien of over $400,000 against the property, which represents the cost the city was billed for limited demolition work performed before the purchase. The city is currently suing Freudenheim to recover those fees. The building is undergoing minor demolition to shore up the remaining structure. Savarino's tentative plans include living units on two floors with parking on the ground floor. Construction could begin as early as this year, but more likely next year. The project is estimated to cost at least $3,500,000, and all plans must be approved by the city's planning board. The city had originally ordered an emergency demolition after Freudenheim gave permission on June 12 during an emergency Preservation Board meeting, stating he would not rehabilitate the building. Residents obtained a restraining order to halt demolition. The next hearing is scheduled for September 2.

reconstructed_article: Australian transport investigators identified a safety issue with engines fitted to Airbus A380 passenger airliners. The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) said some Rolls-Royce Trent 900 engines may be prone to fatigue cracking, which could lead to oil leakage and fire. The ATSB said this was central to the engine failure on a Qantas A380 on November 4, shortly after take-off from Singapore. Qantas grounded all six of its A380 fleet for safety checks before returning them to service. The ATSB said the manufacturing fault could lead to an elevated risk of fatigue crack initiation and growth, oil leakage, and a resulting oil fire. The agency, which is responsible for such investigations, urged Rolls-Royce to address the safety issue and take actions necessary to ensure the safety of flight operations in aircraft equipped with Trent 900 series engines. Qantas stated there was no immediate risk to flight safety but would conduct further investigations. Two A380 aircraft were in operational service, with both to be inspected at the Qantas Jet Base in Sydney. Two other airlines, Lufthansa and Singapore Airlines, use A380 aircraft with Trent engines. Singapore Airlines said it was checking its A380 engines on a daily basis and would carry out the new ATSB-advised checks as quickly as possible. The A380 made its first commercial flight in 2007 and has a maximum capacity of 840 passengers, though Qantas' can carry 450.

reconstructed_article: Australian transport investigators identified a safety issue with engines fitted to Airbus A380 passenger airliners. The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) said some Rolls-Royce Trent 900 engines may be prone to fatigue cracking, which could lead to oil leakage and fire. The ATSB said this was central to the engine failure on a Qantas A380 on November 4, shortly after take-off from Singapore. Qantas grounded all six of its A380 fleet for safety checks before returning them to service. The ATSB said the manufacturing fault could lead to an elevated risk of fatigue crack initiation and growth, oil leakage, and a resulting oil fire. The agency urged Rolls-Royce to address the safety issue and take actions necessary to ensure the safety of flight operations in aircraft equipped with Trent 900 series engines. Qantas stated there was no immediate risk to flight safety but would conduct further investigations. Two A380 aircraft were in operational service, with both to be inspected at the Qantas Jet Base in Sydney. Two other airlines, Lufthansa and Singapore Airlines, use A380 aircraft with Trent engines. Singapore Airlines said it was checking its A380 engines on a daily basis and would promptly carry out the new ATSB-advised checks as quickly as possible. The A380 made its first commercial flight in 2007 and has a maximum capacity of 840 passengers, though Qantas' can carry 450.

reconstructed_article: At the end of January, Bach Technology announced MusicDNA, a new music file format intended as a replacement for the aging MP3 format. MusicDNA uses compression methods similar to MP3 but adds an XML file that defines additional content, including lyrics, artwork, tour dates, blog posts, videos, and Twitter feeds. The files also contain audio analysis information intended to improve search, recommendation, and playlist tools. Bach Technology CEO Stefan Kohlmeyer stated that MusicDNA has been in development since the company's founding in 2007. Bach holds a strategic partnership with Fraunhofer IDMT, whose CEO Karlheinz Brandenburg, credited with inventing the MP3, participates in research and development discussions. Unlike iTunes LP, MusicDNA is built on open standards and is platform-agnostic, allowing transfer between devices and purchase of individual tracks rather than complete albums. Additional content updates dynamically when the user is online. Only paid files receive dynamic updates, which Bach Technology describes as an incentive to purchase legitimate files rather than using peer-to-peer networks. Mark Mulligan, vice president and research director at Forrester Research, told a UK newspaper that innovations like iTunes LP need to go further, suggesting people should pay once for regularly updated content. Kohlmeyer noted that MP3 was developed over twenty years ago and does little to add to the listening experience beyond portability. MusicDNA rollout is staggered over 2010, with beta versions around Easter and full commercial rollout expected in summer.

Alan Winters, professor of economics at the University of Sussex and founding director of the UK Trade Policy Observatory (UKTPO), was interviewed about UK trade policy following Brexit. Winters said he was opposed to Brexit and considers it poor economic policy, arguing the UK would have been better off with a tighter relationship with Europe to keep trade costs lower. He co-authored reports including "The Costs of Brexit," "COVID-19 will reinforce the Brexit shock," and "Taking stock of the new UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement." Winters said Brexit and COVID-19 shocks interact, making recovery from lost export markets harder. He dismissed the idea that trade with distant partners like Australia, New Zealand, or CPTPP members could replace EU trade, noting the EU represents approximately half of UK trade and that benefits of trade agreements weaken with distance. On fishing, he noted the UK gained some quota transfer but must still prove compliance with EU standards to sell fish in Europe. He criticized government statistics presenting 218 billion in rolled-over trade as new income. Regarding the Northern Ireland Protocol, he attributed complications to Brexit and the specific form of Brexit chosen by Boris Johnson. Winters argued the UK should pursue a quiet, cooperative role in the WTO and urged the G7 to focus on repairing the multilateral trading system rather than pursuing bilateral photo opportunities. He expressed concern about rising Chinese-Western tensions and cautioned against framing democratic cooperation in an anti-China light. Alan Winters, professor of economics at the University of Sussex and founding director of the UK Trade Policy Observatory (UKTPO), was interviewed about UK trade policy following Brexit. He co-authored reports including "The Costs of Brexit," "COVID-19 will reinforce the Brexit shock," and "Taking stock of the new UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement." Winters said Brexit and COVID-19 shocks interact, making recovery from lost export markets harder. He dismissed the idea that trade with distant partners like Australia, New Zealand, or CPTPP members could replace EU trade, noting the EU represents approximately half of UK trade and that benefits of trade agreements weaken with distance. On fishing, he noted the UK gained some quota transfer but must still prove compliance with EU standards to sell fish in Europe. He took issue with government statistics presenting 218 billion in rolled-over trade as new income. Regarding the Northern Ireland Protocol, he attributed complications to Brexit and the specific form of Brexit chosen by Boris Johnson. Winters argued the UK should pursue a quiet, cooperative role in the WTO and urged the G7 to focus on repairing the multilateral trading system rather than pursuing bilateral photo opportunities. He expressed concern about rising Chinese-Western tensions and cautioned against framing democratic cooperation in an anti-China light. He called for greater domestic debate on trade policy, noting the executive faces few constraints.

U.S. officials announced new plans requiring air traffic controllers to have longer rest periods between shifts, following a series of incidents in which controllers fell asleep on duty at airports across the country. Transport Secretary LaHood said he was outraged by the incidents. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), the U.S. government agency responsible for aviation, said the plans would be implemented immediately.

The announcement came after another controller was suspended this week for falling asleep while directing aircraft near [location]. This was the sixth such incident this year, with controllers having fallen asleep in Nevada, Washington D.C., and Tennessee. In one incident, two commercial passenger jets landed without direction from the control tower because the controller had fallen asleep.

Under the new plans, controllers must have a minimum of nine hours rest between shifts, an increase of one hour. More supervisors will be required during night shifts, and controllers will be restricted in what shifts they can swap with colleagues. LaHood said controllers who fall asleep on duty will face consequences.

Earlier this week, the head of the air traffic organization at the FAA resigned after LaHood called the crisis unacceptable. The results of a study on how fatigue affects controllers will soon be published, and the FAA may make further changes. The union representing controllers in the U.S. said it had full support for the new steps.

reconstructed_article: Roger D. Kornberg of the United States won the 2006 Nobel Prize for chemistry for his studies of the molecular basis of eukaryotic transcription. Kornberg's work explains how information encoded in DNA is used to produce the proteins that keep cells functioning. Eukaryotes are multi-celled organisms, such as animals, plants and fungi, which have their genetic material stored in nuclei within their cells. To use their genetic information, eukaryotes extract bits of the coded information via the formation of messenger RNA, which consists of copies of a particular gene within the DNA strand. Translation takes place when proteins are built from the information transcribed with the messenger RNA. Eukaryotic transcription is vital for life. If transcription is interrupted, as can happen when cells are exposed to certain toxins, the cells will die. Kornberg documented eukaryotic transcription with snapshots of the process in action. He created the snapshots by crystallizing cellular material partway through transcription and exposing them to x-rays that produced patterns revealing the intermediate structures. Kornberg's work may lead to novel drugs and medical treatments. Kornberg's father Arthur Kornberg won the Nobel Prize in physiology and medicine in 1959 for explaining how organisms synthesize DNA from nucleotides.

Anna Kenny, a spokesperson for the New Zealand trade union, said concerns were raised about plumes of dust Friday morning suspected to be asbestos, but there has been no confirmation. reconstructed_article: On Friday, 178 plaintiffs, including construction workers and family members of deceased workers, filed a lawsuit in Tokyo, Japan, seeking approximately 6.6 billion yen (about 64 million USD) in damages from the Japanese government and 46 building manufacturers. According to reports, the class action is the first in Japan related to health damages caused by asbestos exposure at construction sites. The plaintiffs are from Tokyo and surrounding areas. They claim the government and manufacturers knew of the dangers of asbestos inhalation but failed to take proper precautions, including ceasing to promote asbestos as a cheap construction material and banning its production. After inhaling asbestos in the workplace, 172 people developed lung cancer or mesothelioma, and nearly half of those afflicted have died. Plaintiffs argue the government and health ministry did not act quickly enough after international organizations issued warnings in 1972 that asbestos could be a carcinogen. They also blame the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry for sanctioning asbestos use under the Factory Act, and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism for approving asbestos-containing materials under Japan's Building Standards Law. Approximately 40 construction workers plan to file a similar lawsuit in June. Following a 2005 revelation that residents near a factory developed asbestos-related diseases, the government implemented a 2006 law providing monetary assistance to victims and relatives. Plaintiffs argue the assistance is insufficient. Japan banned the spraying of asbestos in 1975.

The Senate Intelligence Committee is considering three possibilities: the weapons were moved, CIA intelligence was flawed, or satisfactory intelligence was mishandled by the administration. The last possibility has not been formally investigated.

The ATSB said the manufacturing fault could lead to an elevated risk of fatigue crack initiation and growth, oil leakage, and a resulting oil fire. Transport Secretary LaHood said he was outraged by the incidents. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), the U.S. government agency responsible for aviation, said the plans would be implemented immediately. The announcement came after another controller was suspended this week for falling asleep while directing aircraft near [location]. This was the sixth such incident this year, with controllers having fallen asleep in Nevada, Washington D.C., and Tennessee. In one incident, two commercial passenger jets landed without direction from the control tower because the controller had fallen asleep. Under the new plans from the Department of Transportation, controllers must have a minimum of nine hours rest between shifts, an increase of one hour. More supervisors will be required during night shifts, and controllers will be restricted in what shifts they can swap with colleagues. LaHood said controllers who fall asleep on duty will face consequences. Earlier this week, the head of the air traffic organization at the FAA resigned after LaHood called the crisis unacceptable. The results of a study on how fatigue affects controllers will soon be published, and the FAA may make further changes. The union representing controllers in the U.S. said it had full support for the new steps.

reconstructed_article: George Smoot of the United States and John Mather of NASA shared the 2006 Nobel Prize in Physics for their discovery of the blackbody form and anisotropy of the cosmic microwave background radiation. The Nobel Prize Committee cited the physicists for their work on the Cosmic Background Explorer (COBE) project. COBE revealed fluctuations in faint microwave signals from space that are thought to be remnants of the Big Bang. Although the precise origin of the fluctuations in the cosmic microwave background is not yet clear, they may represent clumps in the very early universe that led to the galaxies seen today. Prior to the COBE map of the universe, it was unclear why the universe contained stars and galaxies rather than an evenly distributed dust cloud. Theorists had predicted that a sensitive measurement of microwaves from the sky would reveal minute temperature fluctuations, which represent variations in the density of matter in the early universe. The denser portions served as seeds for galaxies that formed later. COBE was the first experiment sensitive enough to confirm the predicted temperature variations encoded in the map of the microwave background. The initial discovery of the Cosmic Microwave Background by Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson led to their award of the 1978 Nobel Prize in physics. Although they measured the approximate temperature of the universe to be about 3.5 kelvins, their ground-based microwave telescope could not pick out the detail that Smoot and Mather achieved through COBE.

reconstructed_article: The World Bank released its 2012 World Development Report on Gender Equality and Development. The report mentions India over 300 times, compared with Spain at 48, Canada at 22, and New Zealand at 15. The report states that gender equality contributes to productivity, outcomes for the next generation, and representative decision making. In India, improved local-level gender equality correlated with improvements in sanitation, water supplies, irrigation, and schools. Nationally, a woman's income correlated positively with years her children spent in school. No gender gap exists in attendance for the richest 20% of Indian families, but males outnumber females 5 to 1 among the poorest 20%. Girls in the bottom 20% average completion of Grade 1; males average Grade 6. By age 15, parents in Andhra Pradesh prioritize outcomes for male children over female ones. Indian women earn $0.64 for every $1 earned by men, compared with $0.62 in Germany, $0.60 in Georgia, $0.90 in Malawi, $0.82 in Egypt, and $0.80 in Benin and Mexico. A fifth of married Indian women do not control household spending decisions, an 18% average matching Mozambique, between Nigeria at 14% and Zambia and Rwanda at 20%. India reduced average children per woman from six to three in 35 years, compared with 100 years in the United States. India's maternal mortality rate is six times that of Sri Lanka. Excess female deaths in India dropped by 8,000, from 265,000 in 1990 to 257,000 in 2008; in China they grew by 202,000.

India reduced average children per woman from six to three in 35 years, compared with 100 years in the United States. India's maternal mortality rate is six times that of Sri Lanka. Excess female deaths in India dropped by 8,000, from 265,000 in 1990 to 257,000 in 2008; in China they grew by 202,000.

Sheng-mao Ho of the Ministry of Health told the media that walking is a good recreational sport for health and that the Ministry would present several books to participants to help them manage their health. During the event, a live radio SNG connection was made to some participating divisions, and some magistrates expressed hope that the public would do more recreational sports to fulfill the goal of "Taiwan Walking Day."

The figures were calculated using death certificates from seven states, international estimates of age-specific infection rates compared to antibody test data, and a consumer survey recording deaths. The researchers noted that while not all excess deaths were necessarily caused by COVID-19, the metric can help calculate the pandemic's impact. The researchers stated the death toll was likely to be far greater than the official count and likely to be in the millions. A co-writer of the report said that after the first wave, which was more spread out, undercounting of deaths led to a culture of complacency, but the second wave galvanised Indian society to investigate the numbers. The co-writer added that the figures only went up to May and did not include all of June or any of July, meaning the true death toll may still be undercounted. More than 414,000 COVID-19 deaths have been officially recorded in India, the third-highest total in the world. There is no official record of excess deaths in India during the pandemic, leaving the Center for Global Development's estimates without an official baseline for comparison.

reconstructed_article: International twin-study researchers conducted parallel genetic studies into bipolar disorder and schizophrenia, examining more than 50,000 people worldwide. Eleven genetic regions were identified; seven were for schizophrenia, five of which were previously undiscovered. Two genetic loci were associated with both diseases. The studies scanned genomes of both healthy and afflicted individuals. Researchers found that genetic factors are numerous rather than a single faulty gene. In schizophrenia, at most around 30% of genetic components are thought to have been identified. Pablo Gejman, a lead researcher on the schizophrenia study, stated that one goal of genetic research is to find druggable targets. He identified calcium-activated channels in the brain as promising candidates for new drugs, linked to schizophrenia in the study. A genetic locus called mir137 suggests an abnormality of gene regulation. The team found no evidence that dopamine receptors are involved, though current drug treatments target them. Professor Rodney Scott from the University of Newcastle in Australia noted the strength of the research lies in its numbers, providing robust statistical power. Both Gejman and Scott described the study as highly reliable due to its sample size. Scott noted that the two shared genetic loci are suggestive of a potential common pathway giving rise to both diseases. Gejman called it an excellent demonstration because the same chains are common to both disorders. Each illness affects approximately 1% of people. The diseases are poorly understood, and it remains uncertain whether they are components of a single spectrum or comprise multiple illnesses.

Both Gejman and Scott described the study as highly reliable due to its sample size. Eleven genetic regions were identified; seven were for schizophrenia, five of which were previously undiscovered. Two genetic loci were associated with both diseases. The studies scanned genomes of both healthy and afflicted individuals. Researchers found that genetic factors are numerous rather than a single faulty gene. In schizophrenia, at most around 30% of genetic components are thought to have been identified. Pablo Gejman, a lead researcher on the schizophrenia study, stated that one goal of genetic research is to find druggable targets. He identified calcium-activated channels in the brain as candidates for new drugs, linked to schizophrenia in the study. A genetic locus called mir137 suggests an abnormality of gene regulation. The team found no evidence that dopamine receptors are involved, though current drug treatments target them. Scott noted that the two shared genetic loci are suggestive of a potential common pathway giving rise to both diseases. Gejman called it an excellent demonstration because the same chains are common to both disorders. Each illness affects approximately 1% of people. The diseases are poorly understood, and it remains uncertain whether they are components of a single spectrum or comprise multiple illnesses.

reconstructed_article: The University of Southern California developed a simulation system called Virtual Iraq, designed to provide realistic battlefield effects. The fully-immersive system was created as part of a therapy to help soldiers with post-traumatic stress disorder manage their psychological issues. Professor Paul Sharkey, Director of the Visualization Center at the University of Reading, developed the system together with two professors from the USC Institute for Creative Technologies, Albert Rizzo and Jarrell Pair. They created a virtual room at the Visualization Center where patients can experience battlefield effects. The system provides sounds, sights, and smells of the battlefield so soldiers and military staff experience combat scenarios in a low-threat context. Therapists can add elements to the virtual world, including the smell of burning rubber, the sound of gunfire, and the buzzing of a helicopter. To date, only four patients have been treated, and all reported improvement in their symptoms. Scientists state that the aim of the system is to re-expose patients to relevant traumatic events without re-traumatizing them. They seek to manage patients' emotional responses to make them more flexible in everyday situations.

Gejman called it an excellent and compelling demonstration because the same chains are common to both disorders.

Each illness affects approximately 1% of people. The diseases are poorly understood, and it remains uncertain whether they are components of a single spectrum or comprise multiple illnesses.

reconstructed_article: On Tuesday, the World Bank released the 2012 World Development Report on Gender Equality and Development. The report uses the United States as a benchmark for understanding gains for women globally while noting that US women still lag behind US men in several areas. The authors find that US women are disproportionately represented in teaching and nursing, paid less than male counterparts, and under-represented at the highest business levels, with only 28 of Fortune 1000 companies having a female CEO. Women in the bottom 20% economically have a slightly higher birth rate than those in the top 20%. Immigrants from Southeast Asia and India show higher than expected male-to-female birth ratios, which authors attribute partly to deliberate sex selection based on cultural attitudes. In 2009, over half a million US women were victims of intimate partner violence. US men hold greater pension assets, and elderly women are more likely to live alone than with a spouse. Women account for less than 20% of local police officers and bear 61% of housework duties. High childcare costs disincentivize women from re-entering the workforce after giving birth. The report notes that major gains took considerable time: it took 40 years (1870-1910) to see major improvements in girls' school attendance aged 6-12. In 1921, after women obtained suffrage, Congress passed legislation that helped lower infant mortality from 23% to 15%. Property rights for women began by 1848 in New York. The report cites research showing that higher maternal education improves children's outcomes.

An 11-year-old girl in California faces felony assault charges after throwing a stone at a group of boys who had been throwing water balloons at her. In April, police in Fresno apprehended Maribel Cuevas, and she spent five days in a detention center following the incident. A 9-year-old boy was hit by the stone and suffered a head wound requiring medical assistance. Cuevas has since spent one month under house arrest while awaiting court proceedings.

Cuevas' lawyer, Richard Beshwate, told the BBC: "They [Fresno police] are treating her like a violent parole offender. It's not a felony, it's an 11-year-old acting like an 11-year-old." Fresno Police Sergeant Anthony Martinez told reporters: "We responded. We determined a felony assault had taken place and the officers took the actions that were necessary."

Cuevas is due back in court next month on felony assault charges. During her five-day detention in juvenile hall, she received one 30-minute visit from her parents. She was then placed under a 30-day house arrest and required to wear an electronic monitoring bracelet, which allowed her to attend school. Maribel, who knows very little English, claimed the boy initiated the conflict; the boy also admitted as much.

reconstructed_article:
U.S. District Judge Stein ruled that the use of a 25-second clip from John Lennon's song "Imagine" in a film critical of religion is likely defensible under the fair use doctrine. The film "Expelled," produced by Premise Media and starring comedian Ben Stein, deploys the clip to represent what Premise representative Anthony Falzone described at a hearing as "the most popular and persuasive embodiment of this viewpoint that the world is better off without religion." In the song, Lennon proposes the hypothetical "Imagine there's no heaven ... and no religion too."

On April 23, 2008, Lennon's widow, Yoko Ono, along with his sons Sean and Julian, and music producer EMI Blackwood, Inc., filed suit against Premise Media seeking damages for alleged copyright infringement, as the song had not been licensed for use in the film. On May 19, a preliminary injunction was issued preventing distribution of the film. On June 2, Judge Stein ruled that the fair use defense would likely succeed and lifted the injunction, writing that "the fair use of a copyrighted work for the purposes of criticism and commentary is not an infringement of copyright."

"Expelled" is a contentious documentary claiming that intelligent design proponents are being suppressed by the scientific community. It has received criticism from scientists and film critics and has faced copyright claims over animated sequences resembling "The Inner Life of the Cell," produced by XVIVO and Harvard University. Ono stated that "it is a pity that this decision weakens the rights of all copyright owners" and plans to appeal.

reconstructed_article: Matthew Wright, host of British television programme The Wright Stuff, apologised for remarks made on the show regarding the murder of Liam Aitchison. During the edition broadcast on Tuesday, Wright said "there's been another murder" in a false Scottish accent, referencing the UK television crime drama Taggart. Panelist Charlie Baker remarked the investigation would be like "the longest episode of Taggart of all time," and the audience laughed. Liam Aitchison's family issued a statement calling the comments "insensitive and offensive" and "very upsetting and insulting for, not just the family, but for the whole community of the Western Isles." His father, Norman Aitchison, wrote on the programme's website that he was "disgusted" and asked whether panel members would joke if it were their own child. On the following day's broadcast, Wright said he would "like to apologise" if viewers were offended, stating there was no intention to belittle the tragedy. Channel 5's spokeswoman said Wright's apology was "clear." Wright noted he had not been helped by campaigns urging people to report him to Ofcom, a UK media regulator, and advised such people to "grow up." Channel 5 removed Tuesday's episode from its website. Angus MacNeil, MP for Na h-Eileanan an Iar, described Wright's behaviour as "beyond belief" and intended to complain to Ofcom. Comhairle nan Eilean Siar also complained. A Facebook page titled "Report The Wright Stuff to Ofcom" attracted over two thousand likes. Ofcom was assessing complaints but had not decided whether to investigate.

reconstructed_article: On Thursday, the U.S. House of Representatives voted 269-152 to reject the Net Neutrality Amendment to the COPE Act. The House then passed the COPE Act, designed to make it easier for telecommunications companies to offer cable TV service and strengthen competition, by a 321-101 vote the same day. Proponents said it would lower high-speed Internet prices by enabling providers to bundle phone, data, video, and mobile services. It was the first major telecommunications bill before Congress in over a decade. The Net Neutrality amendment sought to require broadband providers to treat all data equally, specifying a duty not to block, impair, degrade, discriminate against, or interfere with access to lawful content, applications, or services. Its passage would have prevented companies such as AT&T, Verizon, and Comcast from charging content providers like Google, Yahoo, Amazon, or eBay for priority network access. Democrats largely supported the amendment, with 140 voting in favor and 58 against, while 11 Republicans voted for it and 211 against. House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi argued that additional fees would burden small web-based businesses and hamper noncommercial communications. Phone companies and Congressional allies argued the restrictions would discourage investment in network upgrades. The bill is due to be discussed next in the Senate.

Police suspected postmortem molestation, as the body was found unclothed. Purcell police chief David Tompkins stated the motive appeared to involve a plan to kidnap, rape, torture, kill, decapitate, drain of blood, rape the corpse, eat the corpse, and dispose of the organs and bones. reconstructed_article: On Tuesday at approximately 4:00 a.m., around 500 melon-headed whales were spotted swimming near the shores of Pilar, Bataan, approximately 135 kilometers northwest of Manila. Philippine Coast Guard commander Luis Tuazon and Bataan Governor Enrique Garcia Jr. responded to the sighting, coordinating an effort to protect the animals. More than 100 fishermen and volunteers, along with personnel from the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR), local police, and the Coast Guard, were deployed by authorities and used dozens of fishing boats with engines shut off to guide the whales toward deeper waters by clapping and hitting the water surface. The mammals were initially misidentified as dolphins but were later identified as melon-headed whales by local veterinarian Mariel Flores. Four dead whales were found in Abucay and Tortugas, including two adult females, one pregnant and one that had given birth to a calf that also died. A necropsy by Dr. Lemnuel Aragones of the University of the Philippines found the two adults had damaged eardrums. Provincial veterinarian Alberto Venturina said the adults weighed 250 to 300 kilograms, and the calf was approximately one month old. BFAR director Malcolm Sarmiento Jr. noted this was the largest stranding recorded, with previous events involving only 20 to 30 animals. By 4:30 p.m., authorities and volunteers had guided the whales back to deeper waters. Possible causes discussed included underwater earthquakes, chemical pollution, dynamite fishing, and a sea floor earthquake study conducted by the Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory. PHIVOLCS reported no significant seismic events at the time.

reconstructed_article: The British Association of Dermatologists (BAD) released a report identifying an illness termed 'mobile phone dermatitis,' in which cell phone users develop a rash on the side of their face. BAD attributed the condition to nickel deposits in the metal components of some phones. Nickel is known to cause rashes in individuals with sensitivity or allergy to the metal. BAD asserted that the condition is likely to affect people who spend extended time talking on the phone, with prolonged text messaging or calling most likely to produce rashes on the face, ears, or fingertips. Tests conducted in January on 22 cellular phones by scientists in Rhode Island, United States, found that 10 contained nickel, while the remainder had rubber buttons and plastic cases. Researcher Lionel Bercovitch, MD, stated in the journal of the Canadian Medical Association on January 1, 2008, that phones designed for rugged use often have rubber coating and no surface nickel, while those with fashionable designs often have metallic accents and are more likely to contain free nickel. Researchers noted that prolonged or continuous exposure to nickel can cause severe reactions even in individuals not previously allergic. BAD dermatologist Dr. Graham Lowe said prolonged or repetitive contact with a nickel-containing phone is more likely to cause a skin reaction in those who are allergic. BAD claimed that in the United Kingdom alone, nearly 30% of the population suffers from rashes caused by prolonged exposure to nickel. Researchers recommended that individuals purchase swab test kits to test for traces of nickel.

reconstructed_article: The World Bank released its 2012 World Development Report on Gender Equality and Development. The report mentions India over 300 times, compared with Spain at 48, Canada at 22, and New Zealand at 15. The report states that gender equality contributes to productivity, outcomes for the next generation, and representative decision making. In India, improved local-level gender equality correlated with improvements in sanitation, water supplies, irrigation, and schools. Nationally, a woman's income correlated positively with years her children spent in school. No gender gap exists in attendance for the richest 20% of Indian families, but males outnumber females 5 to 1 among the poorest 20%. Girls in the bottom 20% average completion of Grade 1; males average Grade 6. By age 15, parents in Andhra Pradesh prioritize outcomes for male children over female ones. Indian women earn $0.64 for every $1 earned by men, compared with $0.62 in Germany, $0.60 in Georgia, $0.90 in Malawi, $0.82 in Egypt, and $0.80 in Benin and Mexico. A fifth of married Indian women do not control household spending decisions, an 18% average matching Mozambique, between Nigeria at 14% and Zambia and Rwanda at 20%. India reduced average children per woman from six to three in 35 years, compared with 100 years in the United States. India's maternal mortality rate is six times that of Sri Lanka. Excess female deaths in India dropped by 8,000, from 265,000 in 1990 to 257,000 in 2008; in China they grew by 202,000.

edit_plan.after: On Thursday, the U.S. House of Representatives voted 269-152 to reject the Net Neutrality Amendment to the COPE Act. The amendment sought to require broadband providers to treat all data equally, specifying a duty not to block, impair, degrade, discriminate against, or interfere with access to lawful content, applications, or services. Its passage would have prevented companies such as AT&T, Verizon, and Comcast from charging content providers like Google, Yahoo, Amazon, or eBay for priority network access. House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi argued that additional fees would burden small web-based businesses and hamper noncommercial communications. Phone companies and Congressional allies argued the restrictions would discourage investment in network upgrades. Democrats largely supported the amendment, with 140 voting in favor and 58 against, while 11 Republicans voted for it and 211 against. The COPE Act, designed to make it easier for telecommunications companies to offer cable TV service and strengthen competition, passed by a 321-101 vote the same day. Proponents said it would lower high-speed Internet prices by enabling providers to bundle phone, data, video, and mobile services. It was the first major telecommunications bill before Congress in over a decade.

reconstructed_article: U.S. District Judge Stein ruled that the use of a 25-second clip from John Lennon's song "Imagine" in a film critical of religion is likely defensible under the fair use doctrine. The film "Expelled," produced by Premise Media and starring comedian Ben Stein, deploys the clip to represent what Premise representative Anthony Falzone described at a hearing as "the most popular and persuasive embodiment of this viewpoint that the world is better off without religion." In the song, Lennon proposes the hypothetical "Imagine there's no heaven ... and no religion too." On April 23, 2008, Lennon's widow, Yoko Ono, along with his sons Sean and Julian, and music producer EMI Blackwood, Inc., filed suit against Premise Media seeking damages for alleged copyright infringement, as the song had not been licensed for use in the film. On May 19, a preliminary injunction was issued preventing distribution of the film. On June 2, Judge Stein ruled that the fair use defense would likely succeed and lifted the injunction, writing that "the fair use of a copyrighted work for the purposes of criticism and commentary is not an infringement of copyright." "Expelled" is a documentary claiming that intelligent design proponents are being suppressed by the scientific community. It has received criticism from scientists and film critics and has faced additional copyright claims over animated sequences resembling "The Inner Life of the Cell," produced by XVIVO and Harvard University. Ono stated that "it is a pity that this decision weakens the rights of all copyright owners" and plans to appeal.

reconstructed_article:
A pledge to double the wild tiger population in Asia to 7,000 by 2022 was made Friday by ministers from 13 countries. The commitment came at Asia's first ministerial conference on tiger conservation, held in Thailand. The endorsing countries—Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Russia, Thailand, and Vietnam—are all nations where wild Asian tigers are still found.

In a video address, Thai Prime Minister Abhisit Vejjajiva said the wild tiger is in crisis and that this may be the last chance to save it. The meeting was partly organized by the Global Tiger Initiative, a coalition within the World Bank, along with the Smithsonian Institution and various conservation groups.

Meeting host Suwit Khunkitti, Thailand's minister of natural resources and environment, noted that there were 100,000 tigers across range countries 100 years ago, compared with about 3,500 today. According to the World Wildlife Fund (WWF), tiger numbers have declined due to poaching. Voice of America reported that the animals now live in only seven percent of the territory they occupied a century ago.

WWF representative Michael Baltzer said it was important to act during the Year of the Tiger. Global Tiger Initiative program director Keshav Varma said saving the tiger also preserves habitat for other species and draws attention to issues including encroachment and corruption.

reconstructed_article: Corus, the world's fifth largest steel producer, announced on Friday that its steelworks in Teesside, England, may be mothballed, threatening the jobs of 1,920 employees. The closure of Corus' Teesside operations may be forced by a consortium's refusal to honour a 10-year contract with Corus' Teesside Cast Products, which accounted for 78% of the plant's operations. Corus' chief executive, Kirby Adams, said he was extremely disappointed that the consortium members had taken this action. Business Secretary Peter Mandelson said it is essential that Corus does everything it can legally, and with the government's assistance, to reinstate the agreement. British Prime Minister Gordon Brown said the government was doing everything in its power to ensure that the contract is upheld. Mandelson also said the government was not prepared to reconcile itself to the inevitable closure of the plant. The leader of Redcar and Cleveland Council, Councillor George Dunning, described the announcement as being hit by a mini earthquake. Liberal Democrats including Simon Hughes, Fiona Hall, and Stephen Hughes MEP supported the idea that the government should subsidise wages at the plant on a temporary basis. Hughes and Hall suggested the government should apply to the EU's European Globalisation Fund. Adams said the move could bring to an end a heritage of steelmaking at Teesside. A 90-day consultation period is due to begin, Corus said. Corus' owner, Tata Steel, is also facing difficulties with another UK operation, automobile company Jaguar Land Rover.

reconstructed_article: Since 2006, AutoTronics Taipei has brought together companies from electronic and automobile-related industries. At TAITRONICS Autumn (Taipei International Electronic Autumn Show) in 2005, the Car Electronics Pavilion was established before AutoTronics Taipei's launch, attracting attention from both industries. Yulon Group subsequently organized its sub-companies into a pavilion to showcase automobile parts, accessories, and applications. Modern automotive devices currently include automobile navigation, mobile entertainment, and road safety features. In a keynote speech at the TARC Pavilion, Jamie Hsu, Consultant of the Ministry of Economic Affairs of the Republic of China, identified threats and opportunities in the automotive industry. His remarks echoed a statement by Yi-cheng Liu, Chairman of the Taiwan Transportation Vehicle Manufacturers' Association, who said the automobile industry should not be monopolized by a single company and should pursue optimization and transformation with related industries such as IT and electronics. Some participants had previously taken part in Taipei IT Month, CeBIT, or Computex Taipei, though responses to participation in Computex 2008 varied. Renesas Technology, a participant in Computex 2007, did not showcase at Computex 2008, while Fujitsu and TomTom both declared they would participate in the 2008 Taipei IT Month. Industry participants noted that collaboration across industries is essential to success, as no company can monopolize any industry, even as the automobile industry is expected to become a trillion-dollar industry in Taiwan.

reconstructed_article: After Atlanta, Georgia lost its bid to host Wikimania 2008, which was awarded to Alexandria, Egypt, organizers began planning a Conference of the Americas focused on Wikimedia in the Americas. The conference is scheduled for May 15-18, 2008, at the Georgia Institute of Technology in Atlanta. One organizer, an unpaid intern at the Wikimedia Foundation offices in St. Petersburg, Florida, stated that planning discussions began before the Wikimania location was announced and that the conference was not created in retaliation or to compete with Wikimania. He said the goal is to provide a Wikimedia event for the western hemisphere, noting that travel to Egypt is more expensive for people in the region. Over 100 interested parties across the United States have expressed interest in volunteering or attending. Wikimedia and the free culture movement will be covered by the conference in relation to communities in North America, including the United States and Canada, and Latin America. A journalism segment will be held at the Turner Broadcasting building on Techwood Drive in Midtown Atlanta. The Wikimedia Foundation and Wikimedia Argentina have received proposals for endorsement, with decisions pending. Georgia Tech, the Public Journalism Network, and the Carolina Open Source Initiative sponsor the conference. The selection of Alexandria for Wikimania 2008 prompted discussion on public mailing lists regarding safety, free speech, and the jury's decision process.

reconstructed_article: Police in Purcell, Oklahoma, approximately 40 miles (64 km) south of Oklahoma City, discovered the body of ten-year-old Jamie Rose Bolin on Friday in the apartment of Kevin Underwood, 26, a resident of the same apartment complex. Tim Kuykendall, district attorney for McClain County, said the body was found in a storage bin in the bedroom closet. Underwood was arrested on suspicion of first-degree murder and held without bail, pending further proceedings. He had no known prior criminal record or history of mental illness. Bolin was last seen on Wednesday near the Purcell public library, and her family reported her missing that night. Officials issued an Amber Alert on Thursday night, noting that no abduction had been reported initially. Underwood only came under suspicion at an information checkpoint set up at the apartment complex. Police found a decorative dagger, hacksaw, barbecue skewers, meat tenderizer, and wooden cutting board in his apartment. Preliminary autopsy reports indicated Bolin died of asphyxiation and blunt force trauma to the head. Authorities said deep saw marks on the body suggested an attempt to decapitate her. Police suspected possible postmortem molestation, as the body was found unclothed. Purcell police chief David Tompkins stated the motive appeared to involve a plan to kidnap, rape, torture, kill, decapitate, drain of blood, rape the corpse, eat the corpse, and dispose of the organs and bones. Kuykendall said Underwood reported fantasizing about eating someone beginning a year prior. Authorities believed other individuals, including a woman and a 5-year-old boy, may have been targeted and considered. Kuykendall stated he intended to seek the death penalty.
